articleTitle: Centralized Secondary Control Strategy on Droop Controlled Inverter-Based Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: In autonomous microgrid the inverters are controlled using droop control strategy. However, this controller has the limitation that it leads to deviations of voltage and frequency from its nominal value. This paper introduces a centralized secondary control strategy for the restoration of both output voltage and frequency for a droop technique based primary controlled inverter-based islanded microgrid. In this centralized control scheme, each distributed generator (DG) of a microgrid can communicate with the central controlling unit through a two-way communication network. The proposed controller works on the principle of proportional-integral (PI) type of controller that restores frequency and output voltage of DGs present in the microgrid to their nominal values just after any deviations during load variations. The microgrid test system is established on a MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform, and the capability and operations of the proposed strategy for control is simulated and analyzed under different operating conditions for verification and performance evaluation of the controller proposed for microgrid.

articleTitle: Implementation of Field-Oriented Control (FOC) Algorithm for Brushless DC (BLDC) Motor Speed Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This research paper is about developing a closed-loop control system for brushless DC (BLDC) motors. It focuses on developing a field-oriented control (FOC) algorithm to accurately control the speed of the motor. The advantages of BLDC motors, such as enhanced efficiency and reliability, are highlighted. The FOC algorithm enables independent control of torque and flux, optimising motor dynamic performance. The algorithm transforms a three-phase input currents, i.e., abc-frame into a rotating two-coordinate reference frame (dq-frame), allowing for optimal control of torque and flux individually and improved motor performance. The entire system is implemented in the MATLAB/Simulink environment using a discrete time solver with a fixed step size for the sample time. The performance evaluation covers a wide range of speeds to meet various applications and has been compared with the traditional six-step control of BLDC motors.

articleTitle: Advancing Photovoltaic Technology: Investigating DJ-2D/3D PSCs for Enhanced Solar Absorption
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)

This work takes into consideration the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/(FA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</inf> MA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>)Pb(I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</inf>Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>)/(FA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</inf> MA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>)Pb(I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</inf>Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>)/Spiro-OMeTAD structure. The main goal of this work is to investigate DJ-2D/3D PSCs through variations in thickness and interference defect density (IDD). The study makes use of the solar cell capacitance simulator (SCAPS-1D) for its simulations. Due to its high electron or hole mobility and conductivity, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is considered the electron transport layer (ETL) and Spiro-OMeTAD the hole transport layer (HTL).The device’s two layers of (FA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</inf> MA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>)Pb(I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</inf>Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>) are regarded as its active layers. The primary goal of the research is to maximize the numbers of photons absorbed from solar radiation. The maximum thickness value and the lowest IDDs value both indicate the maximum PCE. Consequently, the PV parameters of the DJ-2D/3D based cells are as follows: FF: 80.01%, PCE: 19.16%, VOC: 1.0715V, and JSC: 22.34mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Model Matching Technique Based Controller Design for Low Frequency Oscillation Damping in Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency domain-based model matching technique for controller design to damp out the low frequency oscillations in the power system. The proposed method consists of two stages to achieve the desired performance requirements in the closed-loop response of the system. In the first stage, a reference model M(s) is designed based on linear quadratic regulator (LQR), with the required time domain specifications incorporated in it. From M(s), a higher order controller K(s) which makes the closed-loop system follow the response of M(s) as closely as possible is obtained. In the second stage, a lower order controller C(s) is designed based on approximate matching between C(s) and K(s) at a set of frequency points in the s-plane. In this paper, the C(s) designed is the power system stabilizer (PSS). Simulation is carried out in an open-loop unstable system taken from literature. Also, parametric uncertainty is considered, and the robustness of the controller is analyzed. Simulation results reveal the importance of the proposed method in achieving the desired performance criteria in the closed-loop response while ensuring the closed-loop stability of the system.

articleTitle: Review on Controlling Flexible Robotic Arm - System Identification of Intelligent Evolutionary Algorithm and Dynamic Modelling of Mechanical and Hydraulic Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Robotics is one of the significant technologies related to "Industrial Revolution 4.0." Robotic arm has got a lot of demand in several industries like manufacturing. It is very important to improve production, output, Return on Investment (ROI), and profitability, and reduce human error. The existing robotic arm used in industries is not just expensive and needs experts for maintenance, it is also very bulky and hard to shift. This is why robotic solution is still out of budget for a lot of small and medium enterprises in emerging economies. Irrespective of those problems, robotics solution is still needed to solve the existing issues related to output quality and workers.In this day and age, a reliable and versatile robot is needed in manufacturing industry. Robots must be easier to operate with less learning curve. Their user interface should be intuitive and friendly. There is a rise in demand for using stronger, lightweight, and more flexible robotic arm in different areas. However, unwanted vibrations can easily affect light robotic arm which may cause problems like instability, fatigue, and performance issues. Eventually, these problems affect highly stressed environment. This study is based on the development of "intelligent evolutionary algorithm to control flexible robotic arm." This algorithm is designed for "vibration cancellation" and "trajectory planning control" with "intelligent evolutionary algorithms" like "Artificial Bees Colony" and "Particle Swarm Algorithm." These evolutionary algorithms have been tested, implemented, and verified with "robotic arm manipulator experimental rig." These smart controllers were found to perform much better than traditional approaches in terms of trajectory control, input tracking, and vibration cancellation.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of Green Energy in the Covid-19 Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Green energy technologies offer essential services, addressing the needs of the 759 million individuals globally lacking access to better healthcare, enhanced education, and affordable connectivity; concurrently contributing to job creation and alleviating economic and energy poverty. Developing economies like India, Africa, and Brazil, still lacks basic electricity facility and high-power cut. As the fossil fuel are on the verge of extinct, the adoption of clean energy holds the potential to save lives and drive sustainable development. To address this, our study employs bibliometric analysis to explore the significance of green energy practices in the post-COVID-19 era in response to environmental degradation.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Control Strategy to Operate EDS
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Electric vehicle utilizes regenerative braking which converts kinetic energy and stores it in the battery for later use. However, there are limitations to the amount of energy that can be effectively regenerated. When the batteries are fully charged, the regenerative braking system becomes limited in its ability to slow down the vehicle. As electric vehicle gain prominence in the transportation sector, their reliable operation in hilly regions poses unique challenges due to increase in high speeds at downhill condition which cannot be compensated by mechanical brakes and regenerative braking operation alone. To avoid excessive buildup of heat in the braking system, we need to have an efficient energy management and dissipation system in the electric vehicles to ensure optimal performance, safety, and longevity of the vehicles. And this paper presents the Fuzzy Logic Control Strategy to operate that Energy Dissipation System.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of a DFT-based Causal and Non-Causal PMU
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) have been on the rise since the inception of the smart grid. Being an integral part of the Wide Area Measurement System PMUs provide the required measurements for the wide area visualization of the inter connected grid. PMUs utilize different methods to compute phasors most of them involving signal processing concepts. Usually computing phasors using PMUs involves a group delay which is directly related to the length of the data window used for estimation. This group delay till recently was compensated using a non-causal approach in which the phasor computed at the end of the window is simply the Referred to the Center (RC) of the window. This approach involves a certain latency which can prove to be a hindrance in case the phasor estimates are to be used for Wide Area Measurement Protection and Control Applications (WAMPAC). To overcome this problem causal group delay compensation schemes are used which involve zero latency. Due to the recent nature of the method the performance of causal phasors has not been extensively covered in the literature so far. Hence, this paper introduces the concept of causal and non-causal phasors highlighting the key aspects of both the methodologies. A DFT-based PMU is designed involving both the causal and non-causal compensation schemes. The use of frequency and ROCOF estimates for angle compensation is also demonstrated. Several key differences between causal and non-causal phasor estimates are illustrated using PMU data available from a simulated 4-machine 10-bus power system.

Author Keywords: IEEE standard for synchrophasor measurement in power systems

articleTitle: Power Quality Event Detection using DWT and Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Power quality event detection is a critical aspect of ensuring the reliability and efficiency of electrical power systems. This paper proposes a novel approach of event detection by integrating the discrete wavelet transform and fuzzy logic techniques. The combination of these two methodologies aims to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of detecting and classifying various power quality disturbances. The discrete wavelet transform facilitates the identification of transient and non-stationary events that are often challenging to capture with traditional techniques. In conjunction with wavelet transform, fuzzy logic is employed to model and handle the uncertainty and inherent imprecision in power quality data. The proposed approach gives the characterization of power quality events by extracting the features from wavelet transform and classification is done using rule based fuzzy logic approach.

articleTitle: Enhanced Control Performance for Higher Order SISO Delayed Time Processes
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The paper proposes a controller for higher order SISO delayed time processes which employs an identical open loop transfer function that is required for an integrating plus time delay transfer function model. The proposed technique's controller settings depends on the tuning factor and process model parameters. The closed-loop responses of numerous simulated case studies are studied. When compared to existing strategies, the proposed method provides better closed-loop performance for both set point and regulatory situations. Evaluation metrics such as integral error, stability margins, and sensitivity peak are compared, and it is discovered that improved responses are obtained using the proposed simple method, which has straightforward mathematical relations of process parameters for controller design. The proposed method has been verified experimentally on a higher order ratio process and demonstrates better performance.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Controller for Conical Tank Process
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Conical tanks are widely used in various industrial processes because of their efficient storage and mixing capabilities. Conventional control methods face challenges in controlling liquid levels in conical tanks due to their complexity and nonlinearity. The use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) techniques is used in this paper to present a novel approach to solving this problem. We propose a DRL-based controller that adjusts the inlet and outlet flow rates to regulate the liquid level in a conical tank system. A reward mechanism is used by the DRL agent to interact with environment and learn to enhance cumulative reward over time. In designing the DRL agent, we consider the actor-critic architecture with the DDPG agent, which is suitable for process control implementation. Simulated experiments are used to compare the performance of the proposed DRL controller with self-tuned PID controllers to evaluate its effectiveness. Based on the results, it can be inferred that the DRL controller is superior to conventional methods in terms of set-point tracking accuracy, demonstrating its potential for practical industrial applications. This controller is superior to PID and other neural network-based controllers because it eliminates the need to linearize the non-linear characteristics, tune PID parameters, and develop mathematical model.

articleTitle: Design of reduced-order observer using AGTM/AGMP matching method
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This paper proposes a reduced-order observer design method for a plant to match its response with that of its full-order observer. This method utilizes the virtue of Approximate Generalized Time Moments (AGTM) /Approximate Generalized Markov Parameters (AGMP) matching and the robustness of the optimization technique in simplifying system complexity. The main objective is to match the full-order observer response as closely as practical to the reduced-order model formulated. A set of linear simultaneous equations is generated for various expansion points and this is solved by optimization technique which ultimately gives rise to all unknown reduced-observer parameters. The participation of the optimization technique for selecting expansion points is compared with random points through their respective performance indices.

articleTitle: Enhanced-Sudoku Topology for MPPT of Solar Photo-Voltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Solar Photovoltaics (PV) are crucial renewable energy sources in standalone and grid-connected PV systems. Static and dynamic approaches are employed for the reconfiguration of PV modules. Static reconfiguration approaches i.e. Sudoku (SDK), Optimal Sudoku (O-SDK), and Improved Sudoku (I-SDK) prove to be efficient and cost-effective, requiring no sophisticated hardware or controllers. Using the MATLAB/Simulink software tool, this research study thoroughly investigates the efficacy of physical reconfigurable strategies under various shading scenarios. The assessment includes how these methods affect the output characteristics’ Global Maximum Power Point, Mismatch Power Loss, Fill Factor, and efficiency. The simulation results show that the enhanced SuDoKu topology improves the power as compared to the TCT configuration under different shading scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Classification Across Multiple Domains: A Novel Two-Stage Self-Supervised Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Self-supervised contrastive learning has emerged as a promising technique in computer vision. Self-supervised learning has become increasingly popular due to its capacity to sidestep the expense associated with annotating extensive datasets. This approach harnesses self-generated pseudo-labels for guidance and leverages the acquired representations across various subsequent tasks. The primary objective of contrastive learning is to ensure that representations of augmented versions of identical samples are clustered closely together while concurrently pushing apart embeddings from distinct samples. In this paper, we propose a novel two-stage methodology, SimCLR+XGB, for the detection of liver cancer and SAR classification. Despite having a limited number of labeled data, our approach achieves high accuracy and surpasses existing state-of-the-art models such as SimCLR+LR and BYOL. In our study, we introduce a self-supervised learning approach for data classification and work on multiple domains such as medical imaging and remote sensing, leveraging a large unlabeled dataset to learn representations of data. These learned representations are then utilized in the downstream tasks of liver cancer detection and SAR classification, resulting in efficient classification and reducing the burden of manual labeling. Our evaluation is conducted on two datasets: the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) dataset and the Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) dataset. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over previous methods, highlighting the effectiveness of our framework.

articleTitle: A VCII based analog multiplier & divider
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: A new voltage mode multiplier/divider using two voltage conveyors is proposed. Multiplication/division is obtained by simply applying the signals to the appropriate ports without changing the topology. The operation is validated in LTSpice using TSMC’s 180nm technology along with a few possible applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Solar Panel Selection: A Comparative Analysis using AHP, Entropy, and Equal Weights in TOPSIS Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Solar energy is only the best capable and environmentally approachable sources of energy, as it has great potential to convert available solar radiation directly into electricity everywhere. In addition, as the cost of photovoltaic (PV) systems goes down, PV becomes more modest with other energy sources and concern in solar panels from companies and individuals. In this study, Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was used to evaluate the solar panels. TOPSIS is applied with three types of weights: Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), Entropy Weights (EW), and equally weighted. The AHP is a mathematical and psychological strategy for multi - criteria decision making. It is a very exact way to determine the weights of preferences. It enables with both qualitative and quantitative parameters to be used in the review process. It assigns significant weights to the responses set of decision manufacturer's preferences. When determining attribute weights for TOPSIS, the entropy technique is usually utilized, and the weight acquired by the entropy technique is always referred to as EW. The observed findings demonstrate the appropriateness and utility of the suggested methodology in resolving the solar panel selection problem.

Author Keywords: Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS)

articleTitle: Computation of Ionized Environment of Unipolar HVDC Transmission Lines Using Gas Bimolecular Collision Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Corona on HVDC line conductor establishes the ionized current environment in the corridor of the transmission line at ground levels. The ionized ionic current environment of high potential dc lines may be categorized by propagation of the space charges, propagation of the ionic currents and enhanced electrical field distribution in line corridor. This paper presents the solution of the unipolar corona equation i.e. poisson’s equation by the estimation of the generated space charge ion magnitude during the corona discharge using the concept of gas bimolecular collision theory. The concept of gas bimolecular collision theory utilizes the ambient climatic parameter effects on the evaluation of the propagation of the ionized current at ground levels which is major drawback of current computational approach. Multiple experimental studies on DC transmission lines are carried out in the indoor and outdoor laboratory of CPRI on reduced scale down experimental models at various high potential dc supply conditions. To the same experimental model configurations, experimental measurements are compared with the computed results developed by the authors. The calculated corona generated ionic current magnitudes are exactly matched with those measured experimentally for both indoor and outdoor laboratory model measurements.

articleTitle: Criticality Analysis of Components of EV Motor Drive System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Because of their zero-carbon emission feature, electric vehicles (EVs) have become increasingly appealing in recent years. However, one of the challenging areas in the EVs is the analysis of the reliability and safety of these vehicles. Since the inception of EVs, though there have been great advancements in EVs, there are still many issues to be addressed. The reliability and safety of these EVs are of great interest and these aspects have rarely been studied in the existing literature for EVs. Another issue of importance of ranking of components in a system from reliability, Maintainability, safety and availability point of view. In this paper component importance Measure (CIM) and criticality importance measure (CRIM) of Electric vehicle motor drive systems (EVMDS) have been carried out for the first time, to the best of our knowledge. Reliability modeling, Evaluation, CIM, and CRIM of EVMDS have been obtained. Prioritizing the components of the EVMDS has been obtained using above-mentioned Importance Measures.

articleTitle: Enhancing Color Accuracy in Virtual Reality: Process Control of DCI Display Using Spectral Sensor and Active 3D Glasses
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This research investigates the pivotal realm of colorimetry within Digital Cinema Initiative (DCI) displays employed in virtual reality (VR) setups, focusing on implementing robust process control facilitated by spectral sensors. In addition to addressing fundamental color accuracy, this study extends its scope to include the unique challenge of maintaining precise color reproduction in the presence of active 3D glasses. As virtual reality technologies continue to evolve, ensuring accurate and consistent color representation becomes imperative for an immersive and visually satisfying user experience. The research methodology involves the integration of a specialized spectral sensor, AS7341, dedicated to capturing the spectral characteristics of Barco’s F80 DLP liquid phosphor projector. Employing a process control framework, this sensor continuously measures key colorimetric parameters such as chromaticity coordinates and luminance levels. Notably, the study includes the dynamic calibration of color settings to account for the influence of Volfoni Edge active 3D glasses on perceived colors. Incorporating active 3D glasses into the measurement section improves the display’s color accuracy. The correlated color temperature for different white points was also studied. The locus of measured points follows the daylight locus closely. The spectral data captured by the sensor are analyzed to identify discrepancies between the desired color profile and the colors perceived through the active 3D glasses. The outcomes of this research have broad implications for designing and implementing VR systems reliant on DCI displays. By establishing a reliable and adaptive process control mechanism, the study enhances visual fidelity, reduces potential color inconsistencies, and improves users' overall immersive experience.

articleTitle: To Design Sigmoid Based PID Controller for Twin Rotor MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This paper presents the designing of variable coefficient sigmoid based PID controller for TRMS. The proposed controller continuously alter the coefficients of controller according to the magnitude of error signal of sigmoid function. The modified sigmoid function used as limiter that limits the variability of PID controller under a predefined bound. The PID controller parameter are k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> and k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> are automatically changes between upper bound and lower bound. The suggested control strategy aims to transform the traditional PID configuration into a more refined and effective PID controller, thereby provide more appropriate step and square response and reduced maximum overshoot compared to conventional PID structures with constant coefficients.

articleTitle: Vibration Attenuation & Control Using Geometric Profiles
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This study investigates the potential for vibration attenuation in mechanical structures. We compare the traditional use of uniform and homogeneous structural profiles with new non-uniform and organic profiles inspired by natural examples like the Woodpecker’s Beak and Tree Bark. Through numerical simulations, we analyze the performance of ideal straight profiles against curved profiles such as convex and concave shapes in strength and vibration propagation. Our findings classify these profiles based on their vibration attenuation characteristics, offering insights for real-world applications where vibration control is critical.

articleTitle: Analysis of Serial Peripheral Interface
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Serial peripheral interface, a term originally coined by Motorola in the 1980s, serves as a protocol facilitating the communication of serial synchronous data between a master device, often a microcontroller, and various peripherals. These peripherals encompass a broad range, including EEPROMs (Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory), sensors, cards and more. Functioning as a full-duplex serial protocol, SPI (Serial peripheral interface) involves transmission and reception of synchronous serial data. This document elucidates the operational intricacies and distinctive features of the SPI Interface Protocol, focusing on a configuration with one master and one slave. In this setup, master device orchestrates communication, dictating the timing and flow of data, while slave device responds to master's commands. Understanding working principles and characteristics of SPI is paramount for its effective implementation in diverse applications.

articleTitle: Linearization of Quadruple Tank System using Taylor Series method and Control by BFOA and PSO algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The Quadruple four tank system is one of the real time complex multi-variable tank systems. It involves various process variables like pressure inside of the tank, level of the tanks, flow rate of the process fluid which flows into the tank system. All these variables are to be sensed and controlled. Difficulty lies in the sensing and controlling of these variables as they are inter linked with one another. Flow rate of the process fluid influences or determines the level of the fluid present inside the tank. The system includes two or more input variables with two or more output variables that can be represented using Mathematical Modeling. Here in this paper, the Quadruple System is mathematically modelled, and the linearization is achieved using Taylor Series method to obtain the transfer function model of the system. Further, a Controller based on Bacteria Foraging Optimization Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization technique is used to tune the controller. The TD (time domain) and TI (time integral) performance criteria are used to assess the overall performance of the proposed controllers using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: AMBA based AHB2APB bridge: An overview
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The AMBA is popularly used as an on-chip bus architecture, widely adopted as a standard for interconnections in SoC designs. Its primary aim is to enhance the reusability of Intellectual Property (IP) cores. It helps in accelerating sequential data transmission through a comprehensive collection of bus signals, posing challenges for the in-depth analysis of embedded systems based on AMBA. This study focuses on providing an overview of AHB to APB Bridge—a sophisticated interface bridge that connects the AHB with the APB.

articleTitle: Decisive unsurpassed arrangement of PV panels for diverse Indian climatic zones
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: World's present fossil fuel-based power facilities are overloaded, resulting in an energy crisis. With the growing global need for energy, it is the need of hour to be dependent on distributed energy resources (DER) which are environmentally friendly. There could be a resolution to this conundrum in solar energy. The Indian subcontinent enjoys abundant solar energy. Solar energy can be harnessed in various types of configurations. Since India is a country with diverse climatic zones, it is necessary to assess whether the configuration of solar panel suits a particular geographic location or not. Not only the testing should be done in ideal conditions but the diurnal weather uncertainty like shading and soiling should be considered as these leads to significant losses. Diurnal weather uncertainty can be detrimental to solar photovoltaic plant (SPV) and it can lead to operational resilience diminution, thereby increasing the operational cost and frequency of maintenance scheduling. This study presents the analysis of solar based DER in four distinct locations across the Indian subcontinent, taking into account the load requirements and SPV injection into the grid along with the effect of shading and soiling considerations. Comparison of each geographic location's incurred loss percentage and performance ratio for the analyzed SPV model has been done.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of feature extraction techniques for power quality disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This research paper presents a comparative analysis of feature extraction techniques for power quality classification. The study centers on a dataset comprising nine classes of simple power quality events generated using MATLAB. Additionally, the power quality signals in the dataset are intentionally subjected to a 40dB noise level to emulate real-world conditions. Feature extraction methods, namely the Stockwell Transform and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), are employed to analyze the dataset. Moreover, the extracted features are analyzed with machine learning algorithms including k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), Decision Tree, and Bagged Decision Tree. These algorithms serve as instrumental tools in the precise classification of power quality events within the dataset. The primary objective is to discern and compare the efficiency of these techniques, thereby offering nuanced insights into their respective performances in the domain of power quality distribution analysis. The paper evaluates and compares the effectiveness of these techniques in accurately classifying power quality events.

articleTitle: Application of Laplacian Teaching Learing Algorithm for contrained and unconstrained optimization problems
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Teaching Learning Based Optimization Algorithm, nature inspired optimization technique based on presence of constraints, TLBO can be used and adapted to solve constrained and unconstrained optimization problems. A brief introduction of using TLBO is illustrated through two different optimization problems. The complexity and the mathematical formulation of both the problems is given and the results are also provided using BBO and the comparative result is shown.

articleTitle: Analysis and Implementation of Electromagnetic Dampers in a Flexible Rotor System Subjected to Viscous and Hysteretic Damping
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The present work explores the efficacy of electromagnetic dampers (EDs) in stabilizing flexible rotor systems experiencing synchronous mass imbalance and internal damping effects. A finite element-based modeling of the system has been presented, where the rotor system is discretized into various disk, bearing, and rotor elements. Damping ratios, eigenvalue plots, Campbell diagrams and steady-state response curves have been shown in the analysis. It has been found that the viscous and hysteretic damping destabilize the rotor system, as evidenced by the damping ratios associated with system modes. However, it has been reported that the implementation of two identical EDs at node-7 and node-9 improves the stability margin of the rotor system. Additionally, the mitigation of steady-state response using P-type, PD-type, and PID-type controllers is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Trajectory Track and Controlling of a Quadcopter using Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: A quadcopter is an underactuated system in which four rotors are utilized to attain control over six degrees of motion. The objective of this research is to investigate the dynamic modeling of a quadcopter. Additionally, a Proportional-Integral-Derivative sliding mode controller (PIDSMC) is presented, which is specifically engineered to stabilize the quadcopter. A substantial component of this study entails the utilization of a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to optimize the gains of the PID controller, with the objective of enhancing the calibration procedure and guaranteeing peak performance. Indicators of evaluation, including the Integral of Absolute Error (IAE) and Integral of Squared Error (ISE), underscore the GA's efficacy in detecting enhanced PID gains that facilitate precise flight path management and quadcopter stabilization. The results indicate that the PIDSMC controller optimized with GA exhibits superior performance compared to conventional PIDSMC controllers, particularly in presence of external noise, sensor noise and random noises.

articleTitle: Decentralized Sliding Mode Control with PI Sliding Surface for Two Input Two Output Process with Experimentation Application
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: In this paper a decentralized sliding mode controller with state observer is proposed which is based on Proportional plus Integral Sliding surfaces for MIMO (multi-input-multi-output) Process.MIMO processes are complex to control because their variables interact with one another. The ideal decoupler is utilized to lessen the interaction between the system variables. Then for each decoupled subsystems decentralized SMC is independently designed. Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) approach is used to determine tuning parameters of decentralized SMC.To ensure the stability Lyapunov approach is used. Simulation and experimentation Results shows the efficacy and effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of Dual-Area PV Integrated Power Systems with Adaptive PID Tuning Using the Sine-Cosine Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The purpose of this article is to increase the performance of a two-area PV integrated power system in terms of load frequency control. In the electrical power system, load frequency control is one of the most difficult problems to solve. There is always a huge challenge in regulating the frequency of a power grid, despite the fact that it is an integral aspect of the grid's operation. Damage to the pricey grid infrastructure and all consumer appliances may occur if the frequency control fails. In this research, a population-based optimization approach is used to fine-tune the PID controller's settings. Results from the SCA, GWO, FA, and GA are compared. The effectiveness of the suggested strategy (SCA) is shown using numerical simulations. Other optimization algorithms are compared to the SCA-based PID controller, which is demonstrated to be superior in terms of overshoot and undershoot value, settling time, and Integral Time Absolute Error.

articleTitle: An Efficient Frequency Estimation Algorithm for Distorted Three-Phase Grid Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This study presents a new frequency estimation unit developed for three-phase systems. The algorithm relies on equidistant sampling and demonstrates better accuracy in determining the fundamental frequency, even in distorted three-phase systems. The method involves independently acquiring five equidistant samples in αβ frames and subsequently combining them to estimate the fundamental frequency. Further, a discrete orthogonal signal generator (D-OSG) prefiltering method is integrated with the proposed frequency estimator to deal with problems caused by high distortion grid conditions. It is worth noting that the proposed frequency estimation algorithm stands out for its inherent ability to successfully mitigate the impact of harmonics. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is comprehensively assessed in the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of Advanced Peripheral Bus(APB) RAM using System Verilog
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The main goal of this project is to design and verify an APB (Advanced Peripheral Bus) RAM (Random Access Memory) using System Verilog and verify its random test, and functional coverage. The suggested architecture involves creating a RAM module that can interface with the APB bus, offering an effective way to store and access data. It is used for the least amount of power input and decreased unpredictability of the interface. Unlike AHB, it is not pipelined and is used to link low-data transfer peripherals with capacity for the SOC. Here we design the 32-bit model for devices on the Master and Slave to communicate. The Design serves as a Slave APB and Testbench as a Master APB. Transports are started by the Master on the Peripheral Bus, facilitating idle, read, and write exchanges. It also confirms the highest possible quantity of slaves. Reaction of slave memory presented in a logical order. The protocol uses a random value to confirm functionality. The same indexed address for a value address and arrangement that are randomly indexed Write and read values together. An efficient and dependable development process is made possible by System Verilog's sophisticated hardware description and verification features. creating an adjustable and modular APB RAM while keeping to the APB protocol specifications is the goal of the design phase. The project's design and verification stages both make use of the System Verilog language to extract synthesis on Xilinx VIVADO IDE and the Aldec Riviera Pro 2022.04 tool. The System Verilog programming was used in the design, which significantly improves Testbench components' reusability, including the ability to create Tasks for a range of test scenarios.

articleTitle: Switched High-Gain State Observer-Based Adaptive Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Control of a Quadrotor UAV with Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This paper presents a high-gain state observer with switching properties to achieve the desired convergence within the predefined time set by the designer for the quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The primary focus of the proposed work is the convergence of the estimated state with the actual state within the prespecified time, which remains unaffected by changing the initial state parameters. The presented state estimation scheme employs a switching technique to guarantee convergence within the specified time while avoiding issues related to singularities. Subsequently, based on the estimated states achieved within a predefined time, an adaptive integral terminal sliding mode control (ITSMC) is employed for trajectory tracking and stabilizing the overall UAV dynamics. A simulation analysis is provided to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed switching observer. Finally, the Lyapunov method is employed for the stability analysis of the presented observer-based control scheme.

Author Keywords: and integral terminal sliding mode control

articleTitle: Analysis of Suspension Beams for MEMS Accelerometers: The Effect of Geometric Parameters on the Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: MEMS accelerometers have revolutionized accelerometer technology with their compact size, low power consumption and improved precision, making them suitable for measuring the motion and vibration. MEMS accelerometers rely on the movement of springs or beams with attached proof mass to detect acceleration. One important factor that impacts how well these accelerometers detect and measure acceleration is their sensitivity. To explore and improve the sensitivity of MEMS accelerometers, the present work focuses on assessing several beam topologies with various cross-sectional forms, such as triangles, slanted squares, circles, and squares using COMSOL Multiphysics software. Triangular beams made of solid material demonstrated the highest sensitivity (15.68 nm/g), but hollow slanted squares exhibited notable sensitivity (148 nm/g). These results highlight how important the beam configuration and geometric parameters are in determining MEMS accelerometer sensitivity. Understanding this relationship helps researchers refine the design of MEMS accelerometers, leading to improved performance and accuracy in motion and vibration related measurements.

articleTitle: Enhancing residential demand response through dynamic pricing forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This study rigorously investigates the impact of demand response mechanisms in daily household operations, leveraging smart devices driven by dynamic pricing. It introduces a machine learning framework tailored for real-time predictive capabilities. The main objective is to enhance user convenience, optimize appliance management, and reduce electricity expenses by analyzing market prices. The focal point lies in monitoring and utilizing essential and non-essential devices, responsive to real-time fluctuations in grid prices throughout the day. This approach involves systematic data collection for training sophisticated models, particularly using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The performance of the adopted machine learning model is validated and evaluated for its ability to regulate device usage in dynamic grid pricing scenarios. Eventually, this study aims to establish a responsive and energy-efficient residential ecosystem, aligning with contemporary demands for sustainable living through cost analysis.

articleTitle: Hybrid Processing Unit for Efficient Realization of DNN on FPGA Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Deep learning methods, applied to solve complex tasks, are increasingly in demand across various industries. However, to reach this, the computational operations depend on specialized hardware accelerators. Moreover, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) accelerators have gained a lot of attention for optimizing neural network operations on FPGA and ASIC devices. Whereas, the particular difficulties when dealing with FPGAs include maximizing the utilization of computational units, memory bandwidth, and DSP block availability. To address the limitations of the DSP block, this study uses a combination of a DSP and a few LUT blocks instead of all LUTs. To make efficient use of the computational unit, the processing element performs double MAC operations using a single DSP block via a SIMD approach. Furthermore, this study employs an algorithm to group the weights of identical values, thus optimizing memory bandwidth. The implementation of this DNN involves a 2D systolic array-based architecture that minimizes large fanout and improves the dataflow of the accelerator. This design has been put into effect with the Xilinx Vivado Tool with Verilog HDL.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Control of the Quadcopter Under External Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The quadcopter is an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) suitable for various applications (environmental monitoring, aerial photography, search and rescue, and surveillance, etc.) due to its adaptable mobility. This paper discusses the mathematical modeling and controlling of the quadcopter. The Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller is used for stabilizing and controlling quadcopters in the presence of external disturbances, including aerodynamic effects, external interference, and wind disturbance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power System Resilience: A Contingency-Based Approach for Integrating Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This research paper investigates the critical need to improve power system resilience through a comprehensive strategy that combines contingency-based load flow analysis and strategic integration of renewable energy sources (RES) at identified weak points. The study proposes resilient solutions that fortify weak points through the incorporation of RES, such as solar and wind, by systematically evaluating vulnerabilities to potential disruptions. The study investigates the nuanced interaction of RES with existing infrastructure during disturbances, providing critical insights for strengthening the power grid. Diverse perspectives on the synergy between contingency-based analysis and targeted RES integration contribute to the development of a comprehensive framework for building a resilient power system. This all-inclusive approach ensures a reliable and sustainable energy future, which is critical for navigating the complexities of today’s ever-changing energy landscape.

articleTitle: Adaptive Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control for Magnetic Levitation System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: A novel adaptive super twisting control technique is proposed for the stabilization of the magnetic levitation system. In the designed adaptive super twisting sliding mode control (ASTSMC) technique, the resistance of the electrical circuit of the system is harnessed as an adaptive law to dynamically accommodate variations in the resistance. The developed technique is then compared with sliding mode control (SMC) and super twisting sliding mode control (STSMC) techniques in terms of control input chattering, settling time, control effort, robustness to parameter variations, and external disturbances. Simulation studies are incorporated to verify the effectiveness and suitability of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Development of Computer Vision based Three Omni-Wheeled Wireless Dual Axis Plotting Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: In this paper, a three-wheeled omnidirectional robot is presented for drawing figures wirelessly in the dual-axis plane. This model emphasizes using the Robot Operating system and computer vision algorithms to plot 2D images and the locus of parametric functions on a 2D plane. The omnidirectional wheels with three degrees of freedom provide a significant advantage compared to standard differential wheels with only two degrees of freedom. The design integrates a microcontroller for the precise control of stepper motors, facilitated by dedicated motor drivers in the robot’s system. The images and functions are converted to waypoints using contour detection techniques and finding the locus of the function respectively. The localization is performed using ArUco markers which contribute to the inverse kinematics to get the three individual wheel velocities. With the help of wireless communication, these wheel velocities are transmitted to the robot to reach the goal position to draw shapes. Performing camera calibration and warp perspective transform on the arena contributes to enhancing the consistency and accuracy of the drawing. These factors help the robot to move easily and steadily in an omnidirectional motion for plotting the images and functions and thus, it remains independent of its immediate surroundings for mobility.

articleTitle: Securing Vehicle-to-Cloud Communication: A Lightweight Approach with SCDSA
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) pertains to a network of interconnected objects and the corresponding technology that enables these objects to communicate with each other, as well as with the cloud. Vehicle-to-Cloud (V2C) is an IoT application that facilitates interaction between automobiles and the cloud. Through this connection, various data regarding the vehicle, such as its position, driving behavior, and diagnostics, can be transmitted. The V2C technology holds great potential for enhancing efficiency, convenience, and safety. However, it is imperative to ensure the authenticity of the transmitted data in order to maintain data integrity across transactions. While existing digital signature techniques address this concern, there is a need for a more lightweight approach that caters to devices with limited resources. To address this challenge, this research proposes the employment of the Shortened Complex Digital Signature Algorithm (SCDSA). By minimizing reliance on large prime numbers, SCDSA optimizes the computational burden associated with signature generation and verification. The aim of this study is to develop a secure communication system between vehicles and the cloud using SCDSA. In this scenario, information supplied from a vehicle will only be synced with the cloud provided the data is intact and uncorrupted during the transmission procedure. SCDSA might be beneficial in other IoT applications, without compromising security.

articleTitle: Path Traversal and Obstacle Sensing Robot using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This paper details the development and implementation of an intelligent robotic system utilizing the Arduino Uno microcontroller, aiming to create a versatile robot capable of autonomously navigating predefined paths while dynamically avoiding obstacles in real-time. Through the integration of infrared sensors for precise line following and ultrasonic sensors for accurate obstacle detection, the robot employs data-driven decision making processes to enhance adaptability in unpredictable environments. The central role of the Arduino Uno is highlighted as it executes navigation algorithms, demonstrating successful hardware and software fusion. Empirical evidence from systematic experimentation underscores the robot’s efficiency and reliability in complex environments. This project’s practical implementation of Arduino-based control systems for autonomous robots contributes significantly to the field of robotics, offering potential applications in automated material handling, surveillance, and exploration where precise navigation and obstacle avoidance are paramount.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Full Duplex Transceiver Using FSK Modulation Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: In this paper, a full duplex transceiver is designed using frequency shift keying (FSK) modulation scheme that can work at power line frequencies. Full duplex transceiver use at power line frequencies will cater the demands of new technologies. Although various full duplex transceiver designs already available to support high frequency applications, their use at low frequency applications is not yet largely explored. The proposed design aims at efficient transmission and reception of signals with less bit error rate at frequencies less than 100KHz. The carrier frequencies that are used for FSK modulation are generated using phase locked loop (PLL). PLL is used due to its insensitive nature towards noise and external disturbances. The data has been transmitted by using a multiplexer block whose select line is used for the transmitted signal. On the receiver end, PLL is used to demodulate the modulated signal using a comparator. Full duplex transmission on a single channel supporting low frequency signals is achieved with a very less bit error rate and more noise immunity. The proposed design seems to be working efficiently at the targeted frequency range when simulated using spice simulator. LT Spice XVII was used for all the simulations with 180nm technology node.

articleTitle: Design of BLDC Motor for E-Rickshaw Application in Ludhiana City, India
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: With the paradigm shift from diesel/petrol vehicles to EVs (Electric Vehicles), the study of the present technology of EVs becomes the thrust area of research. Electric Motor is the main component of EVs. Proper selection and sizing of the motor is necessary to obtain efficient results. BLDC (Brushless DC) motors are widely used in EVs because of their high efficiency, high power density, high torque and maintenance-free operation. This paper presents the design of a BLDC motor to be made compatible for use in the Baxy Rath E-Rickshaw in Ludhiana City, India. Dynamic modeling of the vehicle accounts for the calculation of various forces acting on the vehicle to calculate the power required. Analytical results have been obtained for motor parameters by using the Ansys RMxprt tool. RMxprt is a leading industrial tool that provides the designer complete analysis of the motor before it is realized in hardware. The results obtained have been verified by using Maxwell 2D and 3D Design. The proposed motor design is rated at 1.1 kW, 48V with an efficiency of 87.5%.

articleTitle: Unscented Kalman Filter Based Short Circuit Fault Diagnosis of Lithium–ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The present research work deals with a short circuit (SC) fault diagnosis method of Lithium-ion battery pack employing Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF). In this method, UKF estimates state of charge (SOC) of each cell of a battery pack and SOC is computed using coulomb counting method. The residual signal, the deviation between the estimated SOC and the calculated SOC of each cell of battery pack, is obtained. Non-zero mean residual signal is observed only under faulty cases. Based on this principle, SC fault has been detected. It is shown that SC faults can be analyzed and detected by UKF based fault diagnosis method.

articleTitle: Pitch control of Marine Propulsion System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This paper focuses on pitch control of Marine Robotic Vehicles. It is a combination of Electrical, mechanical and hydraulic components. System is highly nonlinear, coupled and multi-variable system. Model Predictive Control has been developed to follow the pitch parameter in the presence of disturbances. The simulation results are given using MATLAB.

articleTitle: Effect of Load Variation on Output Voltage THD and Efficiency of Buck Converter Based Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This paper studies the effect of load variation on the output voltage Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and efficiency of buck converter based inverter. Multilevel inverters are capable of providing lower output voltage THD by providing stepped output waveform. According to the IEEE- 519 standard the output voltage THD needs to be below five percentage for low voltage conditions. Buck converter inverter is used to generate different level alternating output and the THD variation is observed for each level with resistive load. Genetic Algorithm is used to select the value of design parameters of buck converter to obtain minimum value of average output voltage THD at each level output. It has been observed that this optimization technique gives better power quality of output voltage in comparison with other reported studies. Simulations are done using MATLAB/Simulink Software.

articleTitle: Minimizing Power Loss: Genetic Algorithm Optimization for DG Location and Sizing
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: In the power distribution system several factors contribute to power losses. Resistance in transmission lines creates heat and that heat represents waste energy leading to power losses. The mismatch between supply and demand leads to power losses in power distribution system. Power distribution system’s power loss minimization is done by a simulated analyzing technique where Genetic algorithm is used for locating the best location of DGs in the IEEE 33 bus radial distribution system. An advanced technique utilizing Genetic algorithm is explored for DG placement and sizing, decreasing losses and boosting voltage profiles in distribution network. The work emphasizes the crucial role of proper DG positioning in improving system efficiency by reducing power losses and optimizing voltage at random buses. The backward-forward sweep procedure is employed for distribution power flow analysis, highlighting the work’s contribution to effective and vital power system optimization by simulating the four cases based on voltage profile and power losses.

articleTitle: Detecting Alzheimer Disease in ADNI MRI Data Using CNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: In response to the World Health Organization's unexpected revelation of over 50 million Alzheimer's disease (AD) cases across the globe, this study highlights the significance for early recognition, which is critical to effective AD medical treatment. The research presents an original method to examining MRI data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), using a customized six-layered Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). This improved model attempts to improve accuracy and efficiency in detecting early AD indications as compared to traditional methods. The CNN's complicated architecture allows for the extraction and learning of complex patterns in MRI data that are frequently undetectable to human interpretation. In contrast to standard approaches such as 3D RESNET, which are known for their effectiveness but potential limits in early-stage sensitivity, the tailored CNN expects to beat these models in identifying subtle neuroimaging markers indicative of early.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of DC-DC Boost Converter with High Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The conventional DC-DC boost converter faces several limitations, including a discontinuous output current, low voltage gain ratio, and potential issues like reverse recovery in the output diode, which can pose risks to the power switch. Additionally, the voltage stress is notably high concerning the output voltage. To overcome these challenges, a non-isolated DC-DC boost converter with high gain is essential. This advanced topology achieves significant voltage gain while ensuring continuous power flow at both the input and output stages. It also reduces semiconductor voltage stress compared to conventional boost converters relative to the output voltage. Notably, this converter is characterized by its simplicity and cost-effectiveness, using solely one power switch regulated via pulse-width modulation (PWM). It offers particular benefits for photovoltaic (PV) panels by maintaining continuous input current and for fuel cells by providing continuous output current. Theoretical equations derived from this converter are validated through simulations conducted in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Design of 400KWp Grid Connected Solar PV System for Bapatla Engineering College
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The paper presents the feasibility and design issues of a 400KWp grid interactive micro solar photovoltaic plant. India is geographically located at 16.77° N and 80.63° E in the northern hemisphere of the earth, which is an ideal location for solar energy generation and utilization. When 400KWp capacity under solar net metering facility at 11kv voltage level. One of the important reasons behind opting roof top is avoidance of land acquisition problem for installing the power plant. The micro solar roof top system produces green and renewable energy. Neither pollution is not created nor is greenhouse gases emitted in the entire operation of the system. The PVsyst software was used to build and simulate a solar PV grid-connected energy generation system in this work.

articleTitle: Enhancing Reliability: A Delay-Based Algorithm for Diagnosing Current Sensor Fault and Employing Tolerant Control in EV-PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: In the pursuit of advancing electric vehicle (EV) propulsion systems, ensuring the reliability of the underlying components is paramount. Preserving the reliability of current sensors within permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) systems is essential for the precise implementation of field-oriented control (FOC) and maintaining superior control performance in EVs. This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing reliability through a simple delay-based algorithm designed for the diagnosis of current sensor faults in EV-PMSM drives. In tandem, a straightforward fault-tolerant control mechanism, also grounded in the delay approach, is proposed to alleviate the impact of sensor faults, ensuring uninterrupted and stable drive operation. The presented strategy strives to enhance the resilience and reliability of EV propulsion systems, ensuring consistent operation under stable maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control. Extensive simulations in the Matlab-Simulink-Simscape platform validate the proposed algorithm, with additional consideration given to a critical EV operational scenario.

articleTitle: Uncertainty aware State-of-Charge estimation for Li-ion Batteries using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Lithium-ion technology-based batteries have facilitated the transition to electrification in sectors like transportation, smart grids, and aerial vehicles, reducing their reliance on fossil fuels. The state-of-charge (SoC), which represents the energy stored in the batteries, is an unobservable parameter that makes estimation challenging and error-prone. It is also highly sensitive to changes in load demand. Therefore, estimating the level of SOC accurately through conventional methods is computationally heavy and complex. This paper presents a detailed study of various deep learning methods, including Dense Neural Net- works (DNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Temporal Convolution (Conv1d), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), for SoC estimation. A hybrid deep learning model, which combines the power of LSTM-GRU-Attention, is proposed. The proposed models underwent rigorous testing with two experiment setups for performance evaluation, attaining an impressive R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.9976. Additionally, the best models underwent uncertainty analysis. The results prove the robustness and capability of the proposed model with a diminutive prediction interval range for confidence levels 65%, 80%, and 95%. Furthermore, Feature optimization is performed between two feature sets, primary and secondary, to ensure optimal SoC estimation while preserving unique information. Feature optimization helps improve the overall R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score to 0.9997 while decreasing computational burden.

articleTitle: Genetic Analysis through Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This review explores the intersection of DNA sequencing and machine learning in the field of Genetic Analysis, with a focus on applications such as alignment, classification, clustering, pattern mining and virus prediction. While DNA sequencing technology advances rapidly, existing algorithms fall short in addressing specific challenges in bioinformatics, necessitating further research and development. The critical areas include handling long sequences, identifying repeated sub-patterns, optimizing edge length selection, ensuring accurate DNA sequence classification, and facilitating efficient alignment methods. The study underscores the need for improved machine learning techniques to enhance the accuracy and performance of bioinformatics tools in genetic research domains. Additionally, it highlights the progress made in machine learning algorithms for virus prediction, with a call for further advancements in predicting a broader range of viruses, such as Hepatitis B Virus, Ebola virus, alongside continued efforts in SARS-CoV-2 virus prediction. Addressing these challenges and research gaps holds promise for advancing our understanding of genetic information and its implications for human health. This work emphasises the use of mean shift clustering to optimize separation techniques as measured by the Silhouette Score. Additionally, it demonstrates the efficacy of the Gradient Boosting algorithm in HCV diagnosis, demonstrating accuracy comparable to SVM but with higher precision, highlighting its potential for disease classification.

articleTitle: Health of Power Transformer using Furanic Compound Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Transformer failure statistics exhibit that most of the failures have occurred before these devices have reached their rated life. Transformer oil in service oxidizes and eventually reaches a point beyond which it is not fit for the intended purpose. In such cases, the maintenance guide recommends replacing the oil. Further, the Insulating paper used in transformers is subjected to heat and is also damaged by the oil oxidation products. Therefore, the same maintenance regime of the oil is not applicable to the paper insulation. Further, the paper degradation is not reversible; and it has been detailed in the literature that the life of transformers, basically is determined by the life of the paper insulation used. The age of the paper insulation is determined by the mechanical strength of the paper and is measured in terms of its degree of polymerization (DP). The traditional method of determining the DP, called the direct method, requires actual paper samples and is therefore intrusive and costly. However, the recently used method which is also known as an indirect method, estimates the DP value from the furan compounds dissolved in the oil. This method in its modified form has been used in the present work to estimate the health of the transformers. Data corresponding to 40 in-service transformers installed by Bihar state electricity board (BSEB) India, has been considered for the estimation of the health of the transformers.

articleTitle: AI Integration in IoT: A Comprehensive Overview of Applications and Implications
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The complex relationship between AI and the IoT is explored in this study paper, which looks at the two technologies side by side and how they may work together. The study delves into several AI-enhanced IoT applications, such as machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, and how these integrate to enhance device and system capabilities. Information transmitted via Data sent and received from workstations, as well as data collected by sensors, will soon be available on the internet. Data storage, latency, channel constraint, and network congestion are all potential issues that may arise as the number of workstations and sensors continues to rise. This study explores the revolutionary effects of AI on several sectors of the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem by doing a thorough literature review and analysing real-world use cases. By discussing the pros and cons of AI integration into the IoT, the study provides useful information for academics, practitioners, and policymakers. Ultimately, the goal of this extensive investigation is to add to the current conversation about the changing world of AI-enabled IoT, therefore paving the way for new developments in this exciting and fast-paced industry.

articleTitle: Advancements in Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure : A Comprehensive Review of Technologies, Optimization Techniques, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This abstract emphasizes the importance of decarbonizing the energy system through the promotion of electric vehicles (EVs) in combating global warming and pollution. As EV usage grows, power systems have issues that can be alleviated by exploiting the vehicle-to-load (V2L) concept, which involves EV batteries discharging into household loads. This study describes a unique circuit layout that enables V2L functionality and has the potential for development into vehicle-to-everything (V2X) applications through modifications. V2L technologies contribute to the rapid electrification of transportation, providing a way to lower grid loads while improving energy system stability.

articleTitle: Solar PV & Fuel Cell Based Hybrid Electric Vehicle For Mileage and Duration Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: In this study, there is a noticeable increase in the prevalence of alternative sources of energy and electric automobiles. As a result, there's a growing need for cutting-edge technological solutions that can increase an electric vehicle's range, mileage, and duration. The determination of this study is to determine whether commercially manageable, low-cost solar energy-based technology that may increase the mileage and duration of an electric vehicle. PV modules can help a car move forward or power its amenities, such the air conditioner, heated seats for the front passengers, and interior illumination. In this study, a hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) based on solar PV, fuel cells, supercapacitor and batteries are proposed. Through a model-driven approach, this work examines the feasibility assessment of a fuel cell and supercapacitor-based hybrid electric vehicle. Electric vehicles are increasingly taking the role of internal combustion (IC) engine-based vehicles on a global scale to reduce pollution, the use of fossil fuels and the effects of global warming. But for electric vehicles, the main issues are battery life and power usage, which have an impact on the EV's range. In order to increase the mileage, duration and performance of the EV, a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) made up of a solar PV, fuel cell, supercapacitor and battery is simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink software. Control logic is used to integrate a Solar PV, fuel cell with a supercapacitor and a battery which is based on the state of charge of the battery. For hybrid electric vehicle, battery, supercapacitor, solar PV, and fuel cell storage devices will be taken into account, and a unique control topology using PI controller will be implemented. In this proposed work, using a hybrid energy storage technology has increased the mileage and range duration enhancement of EVs. The latter showed better performance in terms of torque production, speed variation. The proposed system was simulated using MATLAB/Simulink2O23a software.

articleTitle: Designing of Robotic Arm Decoding Hand Gestures using Arduino Nano
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: The work focuses on developing a versatile robotic arm, combining digital design, hardware construction, and programming using Arduino Nano. The process begins with the comprehensive design and prototyping of the robotic arm using Autodesk Fusion 360, a parametric modeling tool. The robotic arm features and key components such as servo motors, and its construction is systematically detailed. Integration of the Arduino Nano is explored for seamless system connectivity, with a gesture-controlled circuit diagram. The programming logic, illustrated governs the robotic arm's response to input data from sensors, particularly a gyroscope and a flex sensor.
