The robotic arm displays movements across axes: forward (0 to 60 degrees) and reverse (300 to 360 degrees) in motions in X-Axis governed by Motor 1; leftward (0 to 60 degrees) and rightward (300 to 360 degrees) motions in Y-Axis Motion governed by Motor 4; upward (300 to 360 degrees) and downward (0 to 60 degrees) motions in Z-Axis governed by Motor 2. Gripper Control governed by Motor 3, manages gripper closure beyond a flex sensor input of 750 and maintains an open position below this threshold. These precise movements showcase the robotic arm's versatility and controlled response to specific angle ranges showcasing the system's performance, and effective control over different movements, gripper regulation, and lateral motion.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Different Batteries Technology on Off-Grid Hybrid System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: Several rural communities are still living with disrupted power supplies. Consequently, diesel generators are used for getting regular power supply to provide effective healthcare services. Usage of diesel generator not only have deteriorating impact on the environment, but also is an expensive alternative to grid supply. Usage of renewable energy systems with battery are becoming popular solution for feeding such kind of loads in the remote areas. In this work, an off-grid hybrid electrification system (HES) is designed which consists of Solar PV-Diesel Generator-Batteries for the regular supply of electricity to the available load of PHC, located in a remote area of Kaimur district in Bihar, India. Investigation is carried out for five different technologies of batteries Lead-acid (LA), Lithium-ion (LI), Vanadium flow (VF), Zinc bromide (ZB) and Nickel-iron (NI) which are incorporated with HES. An optimum configuration for a PHC has been designed taking all major techno-economic factors and renewable penetration into consideration. Investigation reveals that a vanadium flow-based hybrid electrification system is the most feasible solution with respect to the techno-economic perspective among all considered configurations.

articleTitle: Optimal 1D control problem of Wheeled Inverted Pendulum (WIP) system using PMP approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: This study primarily concentrates on solving the 1D optimal tracking control problem of a Wheeled Inverted Pendulum (WIP) system. The WIP system is recognized as a benchmark mechanical system for investigating nonholonomic systems. We tackle the challenge of guiding a system to a specified distance where a target object is located, and then returning back to its initial position. This endeavor is driven by the aim of enabling the vehicle to perform a pick and place task effectively. Maintaining the pendulum body in an upright position throughout the motion is crucial. To approach this challenge from a variational perspective, we employ Pontryagin’s Minimum Principle (PMP) to derive the necessary optimality conditions which yields an optimal trajectory with a reduced control cost and tracking errors defined via an objective function. We provide a closed form solution where the resulting Riccati equations are solved using Schur vector approach. Stability analysis of the resulting closed form solution is also provided. We also conducted numerical simulations using the derived linear 1D WIP model to validate the proposed theoretical findings in this work.

articleTitle: Non-Probabilistic Uncertainty Modeling for Renewable Power: A Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2023 Second IEEE International Conference on Measurement, Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICMICA)
abstract: With the global surge in renewable power adoption, the intricate challenges linked to uncertainty in renewable power generation have gained prominence. Conventionally, probabilistic methods have been pivotal in addressing uncertainties associated with renewable power generation. However, the efficacy of these methods is highly dependent on the precision of historical data. In scenarios where adequate historical data is lacking, the conventional approach of defining a probability density function becomes untenable. In light of these limitations, this paper presents a comprehensive review of non-probabilistic methods for uncertainty modeling in renewable power systems. By exploring alternative methodologies that transcend reliance on historical data and probability distributions, this review aims to provide insights into diverse approaches for handling uncertainties in renewable power. The analysis encompasses various non-probabilistic techniques, shedding light on their applications, strengths, and potential limitations. The overarching goal is to contribute to the development of robust uncertainty modeling strategies in renewable power scenarios where traditional probabilistic methods face challenges due to data constraints.
